title: The comparison $f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, and let $f^*$ be the pullback of abelian pro-étale sheaves of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star]. Write $\pi_X\colon X\to\Spec\Z$ and $\pi_Y\colon Y\to\Spec\Z$ for the structure morphisms, and let $p_X^*=\pi_X^*\circ p^*$ and $p_Y^*=\pi_Y^*\circ p^*$ be as in [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point]. The natural isomorphism
$$
f^*\circ p_Y^*\ \cong\ p_X^*
$$
of functors $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\to\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ is defined as the composite
$$
f^*\circ\pi_Y^*\circ p^*\ \cong\ (\pi_Y\circ f)^*\circ p^*=\pi_X^*\circ p^*.
$$
The first step is the inverse of the composition isomorphism $(\pi_Y\circ f)^*\cong f^*\circ\pi_Y^*$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp], precomposed with $p^*$. The equality uses $\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$, since $\Spec\Z$ is terminal, as recorded in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point].

proof.text: By [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point], $p^*$ is the fixed inverse-image functor from the point, and $p_X^*$ and $p_Y^*$ are its composites with structure-morphism pullback for abelian coefficients. Thus the source functor is $f^*\circ\pi_Y^*\circ p^*$ and the target functor is $\pi_X^*\circ p^*$. The setting in [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] permits arbitrary scheme morphisms and Grothendieck abelian coefficients, so neither $f$ nor $\pi_Y$ needs to be finite and we may take $\mathcal A=\Ab$. Apply [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp] to $h_1=f\colon X\to Y$ and $h_2=\pi_Y\colon Y\to\Spec\Z$ to obtain the natural isomorphism $c\colon(\pi_Y\circ f)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*\circ\pi_Y^*$. In particular both $c$ and $c^{-1}$ are natural transformations with inverse components.

source.place: Definition: inverse composition isomorphism, precomposed with p*.

proof.text: [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] states $\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$ for every scheme morphism $f\colon X\to Y$, since $\Spec\Z$ is terminal. Substitution gives equality of the chosen functors $(\pi_Y\circ f)^*$ and $\pi_X^*$, including their object and morphism maps. Denote the resulting identification by $e\colon(\pi_Y\circ f)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_X^*$. After substitution $e_H$ and $e_H^{-1}$ are identity arrows for every sheaf $H$, so naturality and both inverse equations reduce to the identity laws.

source.place: Definition: the equality holds because Spec Z is terminal.

proof.text: For a condensed abelian group $F$, define $\theta_F=e_{p^*F}\circ c^{-1}_{p^*F}\colon f^*\pi_Y^*p^*F\to\pi_X^*p^*F$. For $a\colon F\to G$, naturality of $c^{-1}$ at $p^*a$ gives $(\pi_Y\circ f)^*(p^*a)\circ c^{-1}_{p^*F}=c^{-1}_{p^*G}\circ f^*\pi_Y^*(p^*a)$. Compose with $e_{p^*G}$ and use naturality of $e$ to obtain $\pi_X^*(p^*a)\circ\theta_F=\theta_G\circ f^*\pi_Y^*(p^*a)$. Define the reverse natural transformation by $\psi_F=c_{p^*F}\circ e^{-1}_{p^*F}$; its naturality follows by the same two equations with $c^{-1},e$ replaced by $e^{-1},c$, namely $(\pi_Y\circ f)^*(p^*a)\circ e^{-1}_{p^*F}=e^{-1}_{p^*G}\circ\pi_X^*(p^*a)$ and $f^*\pi_Y^*(p^*a)\circ c_{p^*F}=c_{p^*G}\circ(\pi_Y\circ f)^*(p^*a)$. The component composites are $\psi_F\circ\theta_F=c_{p^*F}\circ e^{-1}_{p^*F}\circ e_{p^*F}\circ c^{-1}_{p^*F}=\mathrm{id}_{f^*p_Y^*F}$ and $\theta_F\circ\psi_F=e_{p^*F}\circ c^{-1}_{p^*F}\circ c_{p^*F}\circ e^{-1}_{p^*F}=\mathrm{id}_{p_X^*F}$. Reassociating the three functors has identity components and the same action on arrows. Hence $\theta$ is exactly the specified inverse composition comparison precomposed with $p^*$, followed by the equality identification.

source.place: Entire proof: Both steps are natural isomorphisms, and so is their composite; component verification.
